name: KS-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Estes has a large financial advantage ($1.76M cash vs $73K)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 6%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+12 district, Estes's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets agree at roughly 93% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the forecast stays close to fundamentals at about a 14-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Tyndell within single digits, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ron Estes seeks another term in a Wichita-area district that leans about twelve points Republican at the baseline. He is a well-funded incumbent with roughly $1.8 million raised and $1.76 million on hand, while Democrat Katy Tyndell has raised about $234,000 with modest cash reserves. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price Estes near 93%. The expected margin is around fourteen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
